newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch say too soon to judge new Surinam president.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say too soon to judge new Surinam president.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said on Friday it was too early to decide if the election of Jules Wijdenbosch as president of the former Dutch colony of Surinam would change relations between the two countries.

Van Mierlo said the relationship would depend on how Wijdenbosch formed his new government and whether its first acts "pointed convincingly in the direction of the development of the rule of law and democracy".

Wijdenbosch, 55, who is backed by former military strongman Desi Bouterse, on Thursday became the first member of the former military government to be democratically elected to head the South American nation.
Surinam won independence from the Netherlands in 1975.
"Mr Wijdenbosch has been elected according to democratic rules by the Surinamese people and the Netherlands must accept this," Van Mierlo told Dutch television.
Asked the Netherland's response if it discovered that Bouterse was really in control of Surinam, he said: "In that case the situation would be different, but that is not what I am assuming."
Bouterse staged two coups and ruled Surinam during the 1980s.
The Liberal Party (VVD), one of three parties in the Dutch coalition government, has called for Dutch financial financial aid to Surinam to be cut off in the wake of the election.
But Van Mierlo said: "I don't think would be a good starting point."
Dutch media reports suggest 675 million guilders ($405.6 million) of the 3.5 billion guilders of aid pledged by the Netherlands to its former colony on independence in 1975 is still due.
But a spokesman for the Dutch Foreign Ministry said he could not confirm this. ($1=1.664 Guilder)
